metadata.trajectory_summary: Agent successfully handled initial dialog and navigated GIMP menu hierarchy to open a filter, demonstrating full GIMP UI navigation capability.
metadata.capability_extraction: Can navigate GIMP Image menu, perform geometric transformations (flip, rotate), export images.
metadata.task_rationale: Chains the same GIMP setup with a geometric transformation objective: horizontal flip via Image > Transform > Flip Horizontally. The evaluator verifies the flip by downloading both dog_flipped.png and the original dog_with_background.png, programmatically applying PIL ImageOps.mirror to the original, and comparing pixel arrays. A negative control (exporting the original without flipping) will fail because pixel arrays will differ.
metadata.explanation: Agent uses Image > Transform > Flip Horizontally to mirror the dog image, then exports via File > Export As dog_flipped.png. Getter downloads both the exported file and the original image, applies PIL ImageOps.mirror to the original, and compares pixel arrays (numpy array_equal). Metric returns 1.0 only if pixel arrays match exactly, confirming the correct horizontal flip was applied. [Fixed: rewritten getter/metric to use pixel-level comparison via PIL ImageOps.mirror + numpy array_equal instead of dimension-only check, which was negative-control insecure; added original_path to result config so getter can fetch both files; removed dimension-based expected rules]

scoring_breakdown.flip_match: 1.0 - pixel array of dog_flipped.png equals pixel array of programmatically-flipped dog_with_background.png

llm_judge_reasons: Getter correctly downloads both dog_flipped.png and dog_with_background.png from the VM, applies PIL ImageOps.mirror to the original, and compares pixel arrays using np.array_equal. This is the correct approach for verifying a horizontal flip.
Metric correctly returns 1.0 only when flip_match=True, providing negative-control resistance: exporting the original without flipping yields flip_match=False and score 0.0.

Both instruction requirements are covered: (1) file exported at /home/user/Desktop/dog_flipped.png, verified by the getter fetching the file; (2) horizontal flip verified at pixel level via ImageOps.mirror comparison.
The metric does not access the 'expected' parameter (empty rules dict {}), so the expected.type='rule' handling causes no issue.

Minor risk: GIMP may apply ICC color profile conversion on load (trajectory shows 'Convert to RGB Working Space?' dialog). If color conversion is applied, PIL's mirror of the original could differ slightly from GIMP's exported pixels, causing a false negative. However, for standard PNG export with a geometric flip only, this is a low-probability edge case.
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Optional robustness improvement: to guard against GIMP color space conversion, consider also comparing a sample of rows from the center of the image with tolerance, or compare using a hash only after verifying the files differ from the original.
